The *Kāmakathā* (Kv 8.4) is a debate text in the eighth book (*vagga*) of the *Kathāvatthu*, situated in the *Abhidhamma Piṭaka* of the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records one modern translation in one language and notes a thematic cross-reference to the *Nibbedhika Sutta* (AN 6.63) [SuttaCentral].
According to computational analysis by DharmaNexus, the text exhibits substantial internal text reuse across the Pali Canon, sharing passages with 41 other Pali texts across 341 matching segments [DharmaNexus]. Its closest internal parallel within the *Kathāvatthu* is the preceding discourse, the *Kāmaguṇakathā* (Kv 8.3, sharing segments §0.1–1.10), along with debates such as the *Kukkuḷakathā* (Kv 2.8), *Puggalakathā* (Kv 1.1), *Paravitāraṇakathā* (Kv 2.4), and *Kaṅkhākathā* (Kv 2.3) [DharmaNexus]. Outside the *Kathāvatthu*, it shares notable doctrinal segments regarding sensuality and feeling with the *Navakanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 9), the *Vedanā Saṁyutta* (SN 36), the *Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa* (Cnd 23), the *Magga Saṁyutta* (SN 45), the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35), and several *Majjhima Nikāya* discourses, including the *Mahādukkhakkhandha Sutta* (MN 13), *Pāsarāsi Sutta* (MN 26), *Araṇavibhaṅga Sutta* (MN 139), *Sunakkhatta Sutta* (MN 105), and *Mahāsuññata Sutta* (MN 122) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments of the text with Chinese translations in the *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99, fascicles 2 and 28) [DharmaNexus].
